reviewer.nature: An AI software reviewer under PROVISIONAL_INTERNAL_DOMAIN_AUTHORITY, for nonclinical sporting content only. This record is an internal literature-based sporting judgment, not human validation, empirical product validation or medical clearance. Clinical judgment stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED.
reviewer.independence: Independent of the decision author, the first-round judge and the implementer (SSCTR-08). No self-check is counted.

literatureAccess.statement: No literature tool was called in this recheck and no source was opened. The rulings below are bounded rule-coherence judgments on values already supported by the decision's sources and by the first review's verified reads (SRC01 and SRC02 full text; SRC17, SRC05, SRC06, SRC13 abstract checks; counterevidence Smyth 2021 PMID 34010308, Oficial-Casado 2025 PMID 41631237). Every new condition only withholds or slows; none is a new prescriptive claim needing new evidence. Where a ruling would need new evidence (spacing a test after a race) I state a conservative withholding condition, not a value claimed as evidenced.
literatureAccess.rule: Search snippets, consumer pages and model recollection are not used as evidence.

amendments.asWritten: assessment.P3.stops: reasons SYMPTOM, PACING, CONDITIONS, TIME, OTHER; missingReasonReadAs SYMPTOM; repeatAllowedAfter the four non-symptom reasons; symptom or not tolerated ends test offers for the plan in force and names the existing warning-sign screen.
amendments.sportingJudgment: SOUND. It follows the screening model the decision rests on (exercise-related cardiovascular events are often preceded by warning signs, SRC17): a stop with an unknown reason is never read as harmless, and a reported sign ends the most demanding optional effort for the plan, with no clinical decision taken by the extension. Ending offers for the plan in force (not for ever) is proportionate: a new plan comes from a restart, which goes through the engine's own eligibility and clinical route.
amendments.implemented: YES, with two gaps carried as conditions: the repeat does not check that tolerance was reported (RC-02), and a correcting row lifts the flag at once (RC-03).

amendments.asWritten: Ceilings never made faster: LONG fast edge at least EASY's, RECOVERY at least LONG's, THRESHOLD at least TEN_K's when both are available; only slows.
amendments.sportingJudgment: SOUND. It keeps the effort order of the sessions (a long run is easy effort for longer; threshold effort 6-7 sits below 10 km effort 7-8) and derives nothing harder from easy pace, because it only moves fast edges slower. It replaces 'never derived from P1' with 'never made faster by P1', which keeps the intent of Q5.P1.

amendments.asWritten: estimates.marathon.cautions [MANY_RUNNERS_RACE_THE_MARATHON_SLOWER_THAN_SUCH_ESTIMATES] and assumes [BLOCK_LONG_RUNS_COMPLETED] with their texts.
amendments.sportingJudgment: SOUND and matches the decision's Q7.marathon disclosure word for word. It is supported by the marathon underestimation of the power law (SRC01: median 10 min too fast at k 1.07) and by late-race collapse in recreational marathoners (first-round counterevidence). As fields, a copy layer cannot silently drop them.
amendments.implemented: YES on the estimate, the MARATHON_EFFORT band and the race-day reference (R-07 evidence).

amendments.asWritten: confidence.agingCountsAsReductions 1: aged evidence plus two more reductions is unavailable; the LOW cap stays.
amendments.sportingJudgment: SOUND. Uncertainty from age (detraining within weeks, SRC15, SRC16) adds to uncertainty from measurement and effort. Aged evidence with one other reduction stays usable at LOW with the widest margin, which is still a defensible presumption with its cause shown.

rulings.q: (a) May a result that does not qualify as capacity evidence still count as a long run for the 10 km and half-marathon endurance gates?
rulings.ruling: YES for a result disqualified by conditions (HEAT, HILLY, TRAIL), measurement, effort or tolerance not reported: completed continuous running of that duration does show endurance, and heat or hills make it harder, not easier. Recorded executed runs already count this way (reading R8), and the gate only withholds an estimate. NO for a result reported as not tolerated: a run ended with a warning sign does not show tolerated endurance. Walk breaks stay excluded, as implemented.
rulings.runtimeDiffers: A not-tolerated result counts today (probe8 B: a half reported tolerated:false opens the half estimate 1:45:00-1:59:00 and band 5:25-5:40, while the screen is REQUIRED). Recorded as SSCTR-V1RC-RC-04 with an integration condition; the value for a future amendment: tolerated === false excludes a result from longestRecentRun.

rulings.q: (b) The P1 easy band's slow edge rests on a single slow run.
rulings.ruling: ACCEPTABLE AS IT IS. The easy band is a ceiling only: its slow edge is not a floor and slower is always valid (Q4.EASY, Q4.rule2). A slow run widens the range only in the direction the decision allows, it is bounded to the latest five qualifying runs inside 28 days, and the new plausibility window removes GPS faults. No different rule is required.
rulings.condition: Athlete-facing copy never presents the slow edge of an EASY, LONG or RECOVERY band as a minimum pace or a pace to keep above (part of G.8).

rulings.q: (c) R-11: no outer population limit for longer-than-half evidence converted up to the marathon.
rulings.ruling: Carried as a limit with a binding condition. Value required in a future amendment: longer-than-half evidence whose MARATHON-model central marathon time exceeds 360 min (6:00:00) is UNAVAILABLE: OUTSIDE_MODEL_POPULATION for the marathon estimate, the MARATHON_EFFORT band and the marathon race-day reference. 360 min equals the evidence duration cap of Q1.qualification (so a same-distance marathon is already bounded) and is just inside the 364.9-min marathon equivalent of the 75-min 10K edge, so longer evidence is never treated more permissively than a half.
rulings.condition: Until amended: before any athlete-facing use, a MARATHON estimate whose centralSeconds is above 21600, with its MARATHON_EFFORT band and marathon race-day reference, is not shown; the client shows the session by effort and the estimate as unavailable (outside the model population).

rulings.q: (d) Supplied laboratory values lapse at a hold or a return, as the observed maximum does.
rulings.ruling: CONFIRMED. Q9 withdraws heart-rate zones on a hold, a long break and a return. Values measured before an illness, injury or a time off training do not describe the athlete after it (SRC15, SRC16), and the app cannot check them anyway. Withdrawing them is the conservative choice, and the athlete can supply new values dated after the return.

newFindings.preExisting: Yes: present on bc40218 (journey 11, week 6), not raised in the first round.
newFindings.description: A field test is offered for the week right after a qualifying race declared outside the plan. assessmentOf decides NOT_NEEDED from the capacity of the week in force (cap = now.cap) although the offer targets the next week, whose capacity already reads the race. Reproduce: probe8 A: 10K 55:00 of 2026-10-25 aged to PRESUMED LOW at week 6; a 10 km race of 52:00 declared for 2026-12-27; result: assessment OFFERED TIME_TRIAL_5K on 2026-12-29, two days after the race, while nextWeek.capacity is CALIBRATED HIGH. The decision has no spacing rule after a maximal effort (only 7 days after an adverse or harder-than-target response), so the runtime does not break a written value, but the offer is redundant and stacks a near-maximal effort two days after a race.
newFindings.condition: Integration: the client does not show an assessment offer when nextWeek.capacity is CALIBRATED with confidence above LOW, or when any entry of actualResults (RACE_RESULT, TIME_TRIAL, FIELD_TEST) is dated within 7 days before the offered date.
newFindings.futureAmendment: Assessment reads the target week's capacity; no field test within 7 days after any race, time trial or field test.

newFindings.description: The one repeat is offered after a test stopped for PACING (or CONDITIONS, TIME, OTHER) whose tolerance was not reported; the first review required the stop to be tolerated. Reproduce: probe7 3 (completed:false, stoppedFor PACING, no tolerated) -> OFFERED TIME_TRIAL_3K then TIME_TRIAL_5K, screen not raised. Mitigated: the repeat is offered only when every warning-sign item of that review is actively answered no (R-02).
newFindings.condition: Integration: the test report makes stoppedFor and tolerated required answers whenever completed is false.
newFindings.futureAmendment: An unreported tolerance on a stopped test is read as not tolerated.

newFindings.description: A correcting row (supersedes) clears a symptom or not-tolerated flag at once: the screen requirement disappears in the same review and test offers come back the next week. Reproduce: probe7 5 (SYMPTOM stop, then a row superseding it as PACING tolerated) -> screen NOT_RAISED_BY_THIS_EXTENSION, OFFERED TIME_TRIAL_5K from week 5. A reported sign is a safety fact of the record; correcting the numbers of a result should not withdraw it.
newFindings.condition: Integration: the client offers no correction of tolerated or stoppedFor on a declared result or test (corrections only of date, distance, time and measurement).
newFindings.futureAmendment: A symptom or not-tolerated flag, once recorded, stays for the plan in force whatever later row supersedes the result.

newFindings.description: A result reported as not tolerated counts as a long run for the endurance gates (ruling (a)). Reproduce: probe8 B (intake longest run 50 min, 10K 50:00; half 2:10:00 declared tolerated:false) -> HALF estimate 1:45:00-1:59:00 and band 5:25-5:40 shown while warningSignScreen is REQUIRED. Display only.
newFindings.condition: Integration (shared with R-01): while warningSignScreen is REQUIRED the client takes the athlete to the existing screen before showing any estimate or race-pace band.
newFindings.futureAmendment: tolerated === false excludes a result from the longest-recent-run gate.
